line: You're in 3B, right? I'm Dana, two doors down. I volunteer here Tuesdays, and any other day the crossword beats me.
choice1: Nice to finally meet you. I'm {playerName}.

line: {playerName}. Got it. Fair warning, the building has two group chats and both are mostly about the dryer on the second floor. Want me to add you?
choice1: Sure, add me.
choice3: Maybe later. I should get going.

line: It eats one sock per load. Mr. Ortiz says that's impossible. I've started keeping a list. Eleven socks since March, and one was a good wool one.
choice1: Okay, add me to the chat.
choice2: Let's pick this up another time.

line: Done. You'll get forty messages about one parking spot by Friday. Mute it, everyone does. So what brings you in? Most people just want the printer.
choice1: Honestly, the printer.
choice3: I'll let you get back to work.

line: Then you came to the right desk. But help me first. 14 down, seven letters, 'not in the know.' It's been bugging me since nine.
choice1: Unaware?

line: Unaware. Of course. Ruth does the whole thing in pen in ten minutes, so this stays between us. Where were you living before 3B?
choice1: Not far. Across the river.
choice3: Long story. I should head out.

line: Well, 3B gets the morning sun, so you won the building lottery. The last tenant left a cactus on the sill. If it's still there, it's yours. Don't water it.
choice1: I'll check on it tonight.

line: The new-releases shelf got raided this morning. I hid one mystery behind the atlases for you, if you want it.
choice1: You hid a book for me?

line: Don't tell Ruth. It's the one with the lighthouse keeper. Two weeks, and then I want to hear who you think did it.
choice1: Deal. I'll report back.
choice2: Mysteries aren't really my thing, but thanks.

line: I'm doing tomatoes on the roof again next spring. If you want a pot, claim it now, before the guy in 5A takes all of them.
choice1: Save me one.
choice2: I'd kill anything I tried to grow.

line: Done. The roof key lives with Mr. Ortiz, and he only answers his door ten to noon. I'll lend you mine. Just keep it away from the 5A guy.
choice1: Do you go up there much?

line: Everyone says that. Tomatoes want sun and somebody who forgets about them. You'd be perfect. I'm writing 3B on a pot anyway.
choice1: Fine. Write it on one.
choice2: Let's pick this up another time.

line: Most summer evenings. It's the one spot in the building where you can't hear the 5A television. Some nights half the third floor is up there in folding chairs.
choice1: I had no idea that happened.
choice3: I'll let you get back to the cart.

line: Basil, which works. Peppers, which don't. Last July a squirrel took every strawberry the morning they went red. I watched him do it from the stairwell.
choice1: Does anyone else garden up there?
choice2: Let's pick this up another time.

line: Me, Mr. Ortiz, the Alvarez kids when they're bribed. Mrs. Chen came up once, looked at my soil, and told me everything I was doing wrong. She was right, which was worse.
choice1: What did she tell you?

line: Mulch, and never water at noon. That's this building. Nobody asks for help, but everybody has an opinion about your tomatoes. I like it, honestly.
choice1: It's the same where my family's from.
choice3: I'll let you get back to it.

line: Can I ask you something? You and Mrs. Chen switch languages mid-sentence and I can't keep up. Is it tiring, living in two of them? Tell me to mind my business.
choice1: Some days. It depends who's asking.
choice3: Maybe another time. I should go.

line: I only ask because my grandmother came over from Krakow and never once talked about it. I waited too long to ask her anything. Anyway. Roof, tomorrow, nine. Bring a mug.
choice1: I'll be there.
choice2: I'll see if I can make it.

line: My nephew teaches fourth grade in Houston. After that speech, a third of his class stayed home the next day. He asked me what to tell the ones who came.
choice1: It's been rough on a lot of families I know.
choice2: I try not to watch it.
choice3: Maybe someone has to enforce the rules.

line: The library got money for a second citizenship class. Ruth's thrilled. I just hope they fix the elevator before they fill a room on the third floor.
choice1: Practical. I like that.

line: Haven't seen you in the building much. Mrs. Chen says you're always at the center on Grand. Good, honestly. This place is dead on weekends.
choice1: There's a lot going on there right now.
choice2: I've been meaning to come by more.

line: You're in here more than I am lately. Careful, or Ruth will put you on the volunteer schedule.
choice1: Put me down for a Tuesday.
choice2: I like it here. It's quiet.

line: Oh. Hi. I'll let you get on with it.
choice1: Sorry I was short with you the other day.

line: Hey, neighbor. Can't talk long, the returns cart is winning.
choice1: Good luck with it.
